pointers.sentence: It is a value held for the thread, or for the task in asynchronous code, which `django.utils.translation.activate` sets and every lookup reads (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:activate`).
The time zone in which a datetime is shown is a second value, held the same way and set by `django.utils.timezone.activate` (`django/utils/timezone.py:activate`).

With `USE_I18N` false, the functions of `django.utils.translation` that translate a message or choose a language are bound, the first time each is called, to those of a module that does no translating: its `gettext` gives back the message it was given, and its `get_language` gives `LANGUAGE_CODE` (`django/utils/translation/trans_null.py`).

| the **format modules** | a locale's `formats.py`, under `django/conf/locale/` or a package that `FORMAT_MODULE_PATH` names: how dates and numbers are written in it | read by `get_format` for the active language, and cached |
Translation is in `django/utils/translation/`, formats in `django/utils/formats.py` and the locale packages under `django/conf/locale/`, time zones in `django/utils/timezone.py`.*

For the third it found a language in the cookie that the view `set_language` sets, and did not read the header at all (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_language_from_request`).

A template writes every value through `render_value_in_context`, which converts an aware datetime to the current time zone with `template_localtime` and then localizes it (`django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context`).

On the way out, `LocaleMiddleware.process_response` set Content-Language to the active language's code and added `"Accept-Language"` to `"Vary"` (`django/middleware/locale.py:LocaleMiddleware.process_response`).

It is made the first time the language is asked for, from every catalogue Django can find for it: Django's own under `django/conf/locale/`, the `locale` directory of each installed application, and each directory of `LOCALE_PATHS`.

Behind them stand the translations of `LANGUAGE_CODE`, which answer what the language's own catalogues lack, except where the language is `LANGUAGE_CODE` itself or a code beginning `"en"`; a regional code such as `"pt-br"` has its language's catalogue, `"pt"`, before them ([Message catalogues: `DjangoTranslation`](i18n/catalogues.md)) (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.__init__`).

`django.utils.translation.gettext` looks a message up in the active translation, or, with none active, in that of `LANGUAGE_CODE`, and gives the message back, its line endings made `"\n"`, when no catalogue has it (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:gettext`).

`django.utils.translation.ngettext` takes both forms of a message and a number, and the catalogue's own formula, from its Plural-Forms header, chooses which of the translation's forms the number takes ([Translating a message](i18n/translating.md)) (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:TranslationCatalog.plural`).

`django.utils.translation.gettext_lazy` returns instead an object that keeps the message and looks it up each time it is made a string, in the language active then ([Lazy translations](i18n/lazy.md)) (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:gettext_lazy`).

`LocaleMiddleware.process_request` ordinarily activates the language that `django.utils.translation.get_language_from_request` returns, and puts its code on the request as `LANGUAGE_CODE` (`django/middleware/locale.py:LocaleMiddleware.process_request`).

A candidate is taken where `LANGUAGES` has it, or a more general code (`"nl"` for `"nl-be"`), and a catalogue exists for it; failing both, another regional variant of its language that `LANGUAGES` lists is taken in its place ([Choosing a language: `LocaleMiddleware`](i18n/choosing.md)) (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_supported_language_variant`).

`set_language` takes a posted language, sets the cookie, and redirects to the page `"next"` names, or else the one the visitor came from, translated into the new language where its address has one (`django/views/i18n.py:set_language`).

`JavaScriptCatalog` sends the active language's catalogue of the messages in JavaScript, the `"djangojs"` domain, with its plural formula and its formats, as a script that gives a browser its own gettext ([The language views: `set_language` and `JavaScriptCatalog`](i18n/views.md)) (`django/views/i18n.py:JavaScriptCatalog.get`).
Each answer is cached for the format and the language (`django/utils/formats.py:get_format`).
A string comes back as it was, and a boolean as `str` writes it (`django/utils/formats.py:localize`).

The names of the months and the days are lazy translations, so the one format string writes "maart" for Dutch and "März" for German ([Writing numbers, dates and durations](i18n/writing-values.md)) (`django/utils/dateformat.py:DateFormat`).

`django.utils.timezone.now` gives the present in UTC, and a database backend that keeps no time zone stores an aware value in UTC, or in the zone the database's settings name ([Values in and out: adapters, converters and time zones](backends/values.md)) (`django/utils/timezone.py:now`).

In Python code, `django.utils.timezone.localtime` converts an aware value to the current zone, and `make_aware` attaches the current zone to a naive one, without the form's refusal ([Time zones](i18n/time-zones.md)) (`django/utils/timezone.py:localtime`).
Both need the GNU gettext programs installed ([Making catalogues: makemessages and compilemessages](i18n/commands.md)) (`django/core/management/commands/makemessages.py:Command.handle`).
